chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
The least right of Allah upon you is that you should not make use of His favours in committing His sins.

key_terms.يَلْزَمُكُمْ: It is obligatory upon you / you are bound

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum right of Allah on His servants regarding His blessings?
ai.summary: In Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines the baseline of gratitude (shukr) not merely as thankfulness, but as the ethical stewardship of blessings so they do not become instruments of sin. This principle, central to Shia moral theology, emphasizes that the misuse of divine favors constitutes a form of ingratitude (kufr al-ni'mah), thereby linking material possession directly to spiritual accountability.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 330. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
The least right of Allāh on you is that you should not make use of His favours in committing His sins. [1]
